Given \( x \equiv 4 \pmod{19} \) and \( y \equiv 7 \pmod{19} \), we want to find the remainder when \((x + 1)^2 (y + 5)^3\) is divided by 19. First, we can simplify the expressions \(x + 1\) and \(y + 5\).

Since \(x \equiv 4 \pmod{19}\), we have \(x + 1 \equiv 4 + 1 \equiv 5 \pmod{19}\).
Since \(y \equiv 7 \pmod{19}\), we have \(y + 5 \equiv 7 + 5 \equiv 12 \pmod{19}\).

1. Compute \(5^2 \mod 19\):
\[ 5^2 = 25 \]
\[ 25 \equiv 25 - 19 \equiv 6 \pmod{19} \]

2. Compute \(12^3 \mod 19\):
\[ 12^2 = 144 \]
\[ 144 \equiv 144 - 7 \cdot 19 = 144 - 133 = 11 \pmod{19} \]
\[ 12^3 = 12 \cdot 12^2 \equiv 12 \cdot 11 = 132 \]
\[ 132 \equiv 132 - 6 \cdot 19 = 132 - 114 = 18 \pmod{19} \]

3. Finally, compute \(5^2 \cdot 12^3 \mod 19\):
\[ 5^2 \cdot 12^3 \equiv 6 \cdot 18 = 108 \]
\[ 108 \equiv 108 - 5 \cdot 19 = 108 - 95 = 13 \pmod{19} \]
